provisions.title: Rights of Data Principals
provisions.text: (1) For enabling Data Principals to exercise their rights under the Act, the Data Fiduciary and, where applicable, the Consent Manager, shall prominently publish on its website or app, or both, as the case may be, — 30 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)]

provisions.title: Right to obtain information on processing
provisions.text: (1) The Data Principal shall have the right to obtain from the Data Fiduciary to whom she has previously given consent, including consent as referred to in clause (a) of section 7 (hereinafter referred to as the said Data Fiduciary), for processing of personal data, upon making to it a request in such manner as may be prescribed,— … (c) any other information related to the personal data of such Data Principal and its processing, as may be prescribed.

provisions.title: Warning or costs for false or frivolous complaint
provisions.text: (12) At any stage after receipt of a complaint, if the Board is of the opinion that the complaint is false or frivolous, it may issue a warning or impose costs on the complainant.

provisions.title: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
provisions.text: APIs tend to expose endpoints that return all object’s properties. This is particularly valid for REST APIs.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: The data-export endpoint (POST /rest/user/data-export, routes/dataExport.ts) only puts together the username, a masked email (vowels replaced with '*', so the real stored value isn't returned), memories, orders and reviews. The same Evidence shows the system also stores other personal data tied to the user: Card records (fullName, cardNum, expMonth, expYear), Complaint files, Feedback comments and ratings, and basket coupons. The visible export logic never queries these models. That is the incomplete-export pattern in the positive example, where data is stored but left out of the export. So the user's data access request returns only part of a summary of the personal data being processed. One caveat: the handler excerpt is cut off ('…'), so the exact final response object isn't shown. Still, nothing in the visible code suggests cards, complaints or feedback get fetched later. The user-scoping issue (UserId taken from req.body, filled in by appendUserId) is a separate concern and isn't the basis for this finding.
